mainTopic: Bringing and chopping wood on יום טוב: gathered vs. scattered wood, what counts as a קרפף, and which tools may be used
overview: The משנה teaches that on יום טוב you may bring wood for fuel from an open field only if it was already gathered into a pile. From a קרפף, an enclosed storage area, you may bring even scattered wood. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about what counts as a קרפף. In the גמרא, שמואל rules more strictly: only gathered wood inside a קרפף is allowed. The גמרא explains that our משנה is a lone opinion, which it shows from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about בית שמאי and בית הלל. רבא adds that light leaves count as scattered even when piled, unless a vessel was placed on them before יום טוב. The גמרא then proves from רבי יוסי's wording that he only adds leniencies to רבי יהודה, and the הלכה follows him to be lenient. A new משנה begins: wood may not be chopped from building beams, and chopping is allowed only with a cleaver, not with an axe, saw, or sickle.

steps.title: The משנה: which wood may be brought on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: From a שדה you may bring only gathered wood; from a קרפף you may bring even scattered wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: On יום טוב, one may bring wood from the field only from wood that was gathered into a pile. From a קרפף, one may bring even scattered wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule for bringing wood on יום טוב to use as fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood lying scattered in an open field is something a person does not have in mind to use, so it is מוקצה. A pile shows the wood was set aside for use. A קרפף is a guarded, enclosed area, so even scattered wood there is still on the owner's mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood, here meaning wood for fuel
An enclosed area outside the house, used for storage

steps.whyThisMatters: The two variables here, gathered vs. scattered and field vs. קרפף, are the whole frame for the rest of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may bring wood from the field
only from what is gathered [into a pile],
and from the karpef (enclosed storage area)
even from what is scattered.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Field: gathered wood only. קרפף: even scattered wood.

steps.title: What counts as a קרפף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a קרפף is any enclosure near the city. רבי יוסי says it is any place you enter with a key, even far away, as long as it is within the תחום שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a קרפף? רבי יהודה says it is any enclosure near the city. רבי יוסי says it is any place one enters with a key, even if it is only within the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the word קרפף, and two תנאים give different definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, being close to the city is what makes the area count as guarded. For רבי יוסי, being locked is what matters, so even a distant enclosure counts. The only condition is that it is within the Shabbos boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Shabbos boundary, 2000 אמות outside the city

phrases.english: What is a karpef?
Any [enclosure] that is near the city,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Any [place] that one enters with a key,
even if it is only within the Shabbos boundary.
phrases.notes: He means it can be far from the city, as long as it is not past the Shabbos boundary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key term קרפף from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: near the city. רבי יוסי: locked with a key, even far away within the תחום.

steps.title: שמואל's stricter rule
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that wood may be brought only if it is gathered and also inside a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One may bring wood only from gathered wood that is in a קרפף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from שמואל that is stricter than the plain reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed two extra cases: gathered wood in a field, and scattered wood in a קרפף. שמואל requires both conditions together, gathered and in a קרפף. That rules out both of the משנה's lenient cases.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One may not bring wood
except from the gathered [wood] that is in a karpef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling stricter than the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only wood that is both gathered and inside a קרפף may be brought.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה allows scattered wood in a קרפף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the משנה, which explicitly allows scattered wood from a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: "From the קרפף, even from the scattered wood"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling by quoting the משנה against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said scattered wood is never allowed, even in a קרפף. The משנה says the opposite in plain words. So how can שמואל argue with a משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn [in our Mishnah]:
"From the karpef,
even from the scattered [wood]"!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that scattered wood in a קרפף is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly permits scattered wood from a קרפף, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: Answer: the משנה is a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows a single, minority opinion, so שמואל does not have to follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה follows a lone opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying the משנה represents only one תנא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל is not ignoring the משנה. He holds that the majority of תנאים disagree with it, and he rules like the majority. The next step brings the source showing this.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is [the view of] a lone opinion.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to a minority opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is the accepted halacha, so שמואל contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a lone view; שמואל follows the majority.

steps.title: Proof from the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reports that בית הלל allowed scattered wood in a קרפף and gathered wood in a field. This is exactly our משנה's view, and it is his own individual report.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about scattered wood in fields, which may not be brought, or about gathered wood in a קרפף, which may be brought. What did they argue about? Scattered wood in a קרפף and gathered wood in fields. בית שמאי say he may not bring it, and בית הלל say he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that our משנה matches one individual תנא's version of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, בית הלל allow the two middle cases, which is just what our משנה says. But this is only his report. The majority hold that the הלכה is stricter, as שמואל ruled. The two cases everyone agrees on match שמואל's two extremes: scattered wood in a field is forbidden, and gathered wood in a קרפף is allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the halacha follows בית הלל here simply because בית הלל is lenient. The point is that this version of בית הלל's view comes only from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and that is why the משנה is called a lone opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: scattered wood in a field is forbidden, and gathered wood in a קרפף is allowed. The two middle cases are the argument, and שמואל rules strictly on them.

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a baraita]:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel did not argue
about scattered [wood] in the fields,
that one may not bring [it],
and about gathered [wood] in the karpef,
that one may bring [it].
About what did they argue?
About scattered [wood] in the karpef
and gathered [wood] in the fields,
for Beis Shammai say: He may not bring [it],
and Beis Hillel say: He may bring [it].

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה is a lone opinion
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר describing the argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.title: רבא: piled leaves still count as scattered
steps.stepSummary: Reed and vine leaves, even when piled, are treated as scattered because the wind would blow them away, so they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Reed leaves and vine leaves, even though they were gathered and set down in a pile, are treated like scattered wood and are forbidden, since a wind would scatter them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new ruling about what counts as "gathered" when the material is light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pile normally shows the owner plans to use the material. Light leaves will blow away in the wind, so a person does not count on them, and the pile does not help. They count as scattered and are מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Reed leaves and vine leaves,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּמְכַנְּפִי לְהוּ וּמוֹתְבִי
phrases.english: even though they are gathered and set down [in a pile],
since if a wind picks up,
it scatters them,
they are like scattered [wood] and are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: עֲלֵי קָנִים וַעֲלֵי גְפָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling clarifying the category of "gathered"
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Light leaves that the wind would scatter count as scattered even when piled, and are forbidden.

steps.title: A vessel placed on the leaves makes them permitted
steps.stepSummary: If a vessel was put on the leaves before יום טוב to hold them down, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he placed a vessel on them the day before, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his ruling with an exception: the leaves can count as gathered after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only problem was that the wind would scatter the leaves. Putting a weight on them before יום טוב solves that and shows he plans to use them. They then count as a real pile.
steps.whatToRemember: "Gathered" means a pile the owner can count on. Leaves that will blow away don't count, unless they were weighed down before יום טוב.

phrases.english: But if he placed a vessel on them from yesterday,
phrases.notes: "Yesterday" means before יום טוב began, when he could still set them aside for use.

phrases.english: it is fine.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel placed on the leaves before יום טוב makes them count as gathered and permitted.

steps.title: How should we read the קרפף debate? First possibility
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand the משנה's debate about what counts as a קרפף. The first option is that רבי יהודה needs both nearness to the city and a lock, and רבי יוסי only adds a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asked, 'What is a קרפף?' A question was asked: what exactly does it mean? Maybe רבי יהודה means that any enclosure near the city counts, but only if it has a lock. Then רבי יוסי comes to say: since it has a lock, it counts even if it is anywhere within the תחום שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line in the משנה that defines a קרפף and asks how to read the argument. This is the first of two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a קרפף is 'any place near the city,' and רבי יוסי says it is 'any place entered with a lock, even within the תחום שבת.' In this first reading, רבי יהודה requires two things: near the city and a lock. רבי יוסי then only adds a leniency: with a lock, even a farther place inside the תחום counts. So רבי יוסי is simply more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: A fenced enclosure outside the house, usually used for storage
A lock or key. Here it describes an enclosure you enter by opening a lock
The 2,000-אמה area around a city that one may walk to on שבת and יום טוב
'A question was asked before them': the גמרא raises an open question
'How is it saying?': how should we read these words?

phrases.english: 'What is a קרפף,' etc.
A question was asked: how is it saying?
'Any place that is near the city' —
phrases.notes: These are רבי יהודה's words in the משנה.

phrases.english: provided that it has a lock,
and רבי יוסי comes to say:
since it has a lock —
even if it is anywhere within the תחום שבת, it also counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's definition of a קרפף (Step 2), after the discussion of gathered and scattered wood and leaves (Steps 3–8).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה requires a lock, which would make רבי יוסי purely more lenient.

steps.title: Second possibility: רבי יוסי makes the lock the deciding factor
steps.stepSummary: The second option: רבי יהודה counts any enclosure near the city, lock or not. רבי יוסי allows farther places, but only with a lock, and without a lock not even a place near the city counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe this is what it means: רבי יהודה says any place near the city counts, whether it has a lock or not. Then רבי יוסי comes to say that even a place within the תחום שבת counts, but only if it has a lock. If it has no lock, even a place near the city does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of its question. In this reading, רבי יוסי is lenient in one way and stricter in another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יהודה does not require a lock at all. For רבי יוסי the lock is the key condition: it lets a farther place count, but without it even a nearby place fails. So in the case of a nearby place with no lock, רבי יוסי would be stricter than רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps': introduces the second side of a question
'Specifically, only': limits a rule to a certain case

steps.confusionAlert: Both possibilities read the very same words of the משנה. The question is only about whether רבי יהודה requires a lock. That decides whether רבי יוסי is always more lenient, or sometimes stricter.

phrases.english: Or perhaps this is what it is saying:
'Any place that is near the city' —

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דְּאִית לֵיהּ פּוֹתַחַת, בֵּין דְּלֵית לֵיהּ פּוֹתַחַת,
phrases.english: whether it has a lock or whether it does not have a lock,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְמֵימַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּתוֹךְ תְּחוּם שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: and רבי יוסי comes to say: even within the תחום שבת,
but only if it has a lock;
but if it does not have a lock —
even if it is near the city, it also does not count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question opened in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי makes the lock a strict requirement, even for places near the city.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'even': רבי יוסי gives two leniencies
steps.stepSummary: From the wording 'and even within the תחום שבת,' the גמרא proves that רבי יוסי is adding to רבי יהודה. He gives two leniencies and is never stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the משנה teaches that רבי יוסי says, 'Any place entered with a lock, and even within the תחום שבת.' Learn from this that רבי יוסי is stating two leniencies. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from the exact wording of רבי יוסי in the משנה. It concludes that רבי יוסי is only ever more lenient than רבי יהודה, which rules out the second reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads רבי יוסי's words as adding to רבי יהודה's rule, not replacing it. So for רבי יוסי a place near the city counts even without a lock, and a locked place farther out, within the תחום, also counts. Those are two leniencies, so the second reading, where he is sometimes stricter, is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the fact that it teaches': a proof drawn from the wording
'Learn from it': the proof is accepted

phrases.english: Come and hear: from the fact that it teaches,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל שֶׁנִּכְנָסִין לוֹ בְּפוֹתַחַת —
phrases.english: 'רבי יוסי says: any place entered with a lock' —
'and even within the תחום שבת,'
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads this wording as רבי יוסי only adding to רבי יהודה's rule, never taking anything away.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי תַּרְתֵּי לְקוּלָּא קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: learn from this that רבי יוסי is stating two leniencies.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 9–10 and rejects the second possibility: רבי יוסי is only lenient.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי accepts רבי יהודה's 'near the city' and adds a locked place within the תחום. These are two leniencies.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: רב סלא, quoting רבי ירמיה, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי as a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סלא said in the name of רבי ירמיה: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on what counts as a קרפף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we just learned that רבי יוסי gives two leniencies, ruling like him 'to be lenient' means both count. A place near the city counts, and so does a locked place anywhere within the תחום שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: A קרפף includes any enclosure near the city, and also any locked enclosure within the תחום שבת. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי's two leniencies.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: רב סלא said that רבי ירמיה said:
The הלכה is like רבי יוסי, to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reading proven in Step 11 into a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: both a nearby enclosure and a locked enclosure within the תחום count as a קרפף.

steps.title: New משנה: chopping wood on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה forbids chopping wood from building beams, even a beam that broke on יום טוב. It also forbids chopping with an axe, saw, or sickle. Only a cleaver may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not chop wood on יום טוב from beams, and not even from a beam that broke on יום טוב. One may not chop with an axe, a saw, or a sickle, only with a cleaver.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two rules about chopping wood on יום טוב. The first is about which wood may be chopped, and the second is about which tool may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beams are building material, so they are not ready for fuel. That is true even of a beam that broke on יום טוב itself. Axes, saws and sickles are the normal weekday tools for this work, so they are forbidden. A cleaver (a kitchen chopping knife) is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaver, a heavy kitchen chopping knife

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may not chop wood
not from beams,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִן הַקּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and not from a beam that broke on יום טוב.
And one may not chop, not with an axe,
and not with a saw, and not with a sickle,
but only with a cleaver.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְבַקְּעִין עֵצִים לֹא מִן הַקּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the קרפף discussion ended in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not chop wood from beams, even a beam that broke that day. Chopping is allowed only with a cleaver, not with an axe, saw, or sickle.
